fasterVsCheaper.title: Getting somewhere
fasterVsCheaper.blurb: Uber, bus, train, walking. Whatever the options are.
fasterVsCheaper.hint: Door to door, including waiting. The wait is part of the journey.

paySomeoneElse.title: Pay someone else
paySomeoneElse.blurb: A cleaner, grocery delivery, laundry, a handyman.
paySomeoneElse.hint: Count the whole job when you do it yourself — the shopping trip, not just the cooking. And count the finding: the searching, the messaging and the first visit are hours you spend once before any of the saving starts.

deliverVsCollect.title: Delivery or collection
deliverVsCollect.blurb: Pay the delivery fee, or go and get it.
deliverVsCollect.hint: Collection means the journey both ways, plus whatever you buy while you're there.

parkingCloseVsFar.title: Park close or park cheap
parkingCloseVsFar.blurb: The expensive space by the door, or the free one ten minutes out.
parkingCloseVsFar.hint: The walk counts twice — there and back.

skipTheQueue.title: Pay to skip the queue
skipTheQueue.blurb: Fast track, priority boarding, a seat reservation.
skipTheQueue.hint: Queue time is usually the deadest time there is. Say so below.

eatOutVsCook.title: Eat out, takeaway, or cook
eatOutVsCook.blurb: The most frequent money, time and mood decision there is.
eatOutVsCook.hint: Cooking is the shopping, the cooking and the washing up. All of it counts. Then how many times a week each — they are rarely the same number, and two takeaways against five home dinners is the whole shape of it.

coffeeOutVsHome.title: Coffee and lunch out
coffeeOutVsHome.blurb: Small, daily, and startling over a year.
coffeeOutVsHome.hint: Making it at home takes minutes too — put them in, and the flask or the machine in the one-off field. And if you enjoy the walk, say so.

driveOrTrain.title: Drive or take the train
driveOrTrain.blurb: Fuel, parking and tolls against a ticket.
driveOrTrain.hint: Driving costs more than fuel — add parking and roughly 20p a mile for wear. The train is cheaper to sit on and you can work, but you leave when it leaves.

inPersonOrRemote.title: In person or remote
inPersonOrRemote.blurb: Travel time and cost, against actually being there.
inPersonOrRemote.hint: Being in the room is often worth real money. Put that on the feel slider rather than pretending it's zero.

switchProvider.title: Switch provider
switchProvider.blurb: Energy, broadband, phone, insurance. Admin now for a saving later.
switchProvider.hint: Monthly bill for each, then the hours it takes to actually move.

subscription.title: Subscription check
subscription.blurb: Is this monthly thing still earning its place?
subscription.hint: There's often no time difference here, so how it feels does the work.

groceries.title: Delivery or the shop
groceries.blurb: One delivery a week against however many trips you actually make.
groceries.hint: Count the trips honestly — delivery is once, the shop is rarely once. Add what you spend in there that you didn't plan to, and say below if wandering the aisles wipes you out.

bulkBuy.title: Cheaper shop, further away
bulkBuy.blurb: A trip across town, or a bulk buy, to shave the weekly shop.
bulkBuy.hint: Count the travel time both ways, and the extra faff of the bigger trip, then how many trips a week each — one big shop against three local ones is the point. Any membership goes in the yearly field — a warehouse club is often the whole of the saving.

fixTheFriction.title: Fix the daily friction
fixTheFriction.blurb: The slow laptop, the bad chair, the tap that takes two hands.
fixTheFriction.hint: Ten minutes a day is sixty hours a year. Put the daily loss on the right.

gymVsPayg.title: Membership or pay as you go
gymVsPayg.blurb: The gym, the pool, the climbing wall. How often do you really go?
gymVsPayg.hint: Membership monthly, the drop-in price per visit — then how many visits a month. Be honest: the number you actually managed last month, not the plan. What it does for you counts too — on the cost alone the answer is always whichever is cheaper, which is not why anyone joins a gym.

seasonTicket.title: Season ticket or railcard
seasonTicket.blurb: Travelcard, season ticket, railcard. Break-even on how often you go.
seasonTicket.hint: Pass price in the yearly field, then the single fare you'd otherwise pay underneath — one journey, not a month of them — and how many journeys you make in a month. That is the whole sum: the pass is the same price whether you travel twice or forty times, and the fare isn't.

annualVsMonthly.title: Annual or monthly billing
annualVsMonthly.blurb: The yearly discount, against being tied in.
annualVsMonthly.hint: The yearly price in the yearly field, the monthly price in the monthly one. The saving is real; so is the chance you stop wanting it in month four.

buyNowVsWait.title: Buy now or wait
buyNowVsWait.blurb: Wait for the sale, or have it now.
buyNowVsWait.hint: Waiting isn't free — count the weeks you go without it, and whether the sale is a sure thing.

extendedWarranty.title: Warranty or add-on
extendedWarranty.blurb: Extended warranty, insurance add-on, protection plan.
extendedWarranty.hint: Leave the cover's time at zero, then say below how likely and how bad a failure would be. The maths does the rest.

claimVsPay.title: Claim, or pay it yourself
claimVsPay.blurb: The excess and the premium rise, against the repair bill.
claimVsPay.setupLabel: Paid now — excess or repair bill
claimVsPay.hint: The excess or the repair bill in the one-off field, then what the claim adds to your premium each year underneath. Then set how long you'll be paying it.

buyOrRent.title: Buy it or rent it
buyOrRent.blurb: Tools, a van, a suit, a carpet cleaner. How many times will you use it?
buyOrRent.hint: Owning also costs storage and upkeep. Renting costs a trip there and back each time.

buyOutrightVsSubscribe.title: Buy outright or subscribe
buyOutrightVsSubscribe.blurb: Pay once and own it, or pay every month for as long as you use it.
buyOutrightVsSubscribe.hint: Purchase price in the one-off field, the subscription underneath. Then stretch the horizon — a subscription with no end date is the whole point.

costPerUse.title: Is it worth buying?
costPerUse.blurb: Clothes, kit, gadgets. The price matters far less than the cost per wear.
costPerUse.hint: Price in the field above, how often you'd use it below, and how long it'd last in "Counted over". A £120 coat worn weekly for five years is 46p a wear; worn twice it's £60.

paysYouBack.title: Something that keeps paying
paysYouBack.blurb: A tool, a machine, an automation. Pay once, and it works while you don't.
paysYouBack.setupLabel: Cost to buy or set up
paysYouBack.hint: Cost up front on the left, then on the right what carrying on as you are costs you every week — the time it takes, the money it eats. Stretch the horizon: the whole point is that it keeps going without you.

buyOnceBetterForever.title: Buy once, better forever
buyOnceBetterForever.blurb: Blackout curtains, floor lamps, a decent mattress. Small money, permanently better days.
buyOnceBetterForever.hint: Cost up front on the left. On the right, what leaving things as they are costs you every day — the minutes, the faff, what it does to your sleep. These look marginal over a year and obvious over ten, so set the horizon honestly.

payForSpeed.title: Pay to make it faster
payForSpeed.blurb: Fast-track passport, express visa, next-day anything.
payForSpeed.hint: The fee and the form-filling go in the fields — not the waiting, which costs you no hours. Then what happens if it doesn't come in time: paying to skip the queue is nearly always about a date that can't move, and if there isn't one, there's usually no case for the fee.

buyRepairDoWithout.title: Repair or replace
buyRepairDoWithout.blurb: Fix the old one, buy a new one, or manage without.
buyRepairDoWithout.hint: What each costs today, and how long each one buys you — with a repair that second question is the whole decision. Hours in the one-off time: waiting in for the repair, researching the replacement. The yearly field is for running costs, if they differ.

returnAnItem.title: Return it, or keep it
returnAnItem.blurb: Is the trip to the post office worth the refund?
returnAnItem.hint: Packing, printing the label and the queue all count.

experience.title: Experience vs saving it
experience.blurb: A gig, a trip, a long lunch with someone you love.
experience.hint: Time here means the getting-there and getting-home, not the experience itself — that's what you're paying for, and it belongs on the feel slider. Be honest with that slider. This is the decision where it should win.

socialEvent.title: Go out, or stay in
socialEvent.blurb: The pub, a party, someone's birthday. Rarely about the money.
socialEvent.hint: Time here means the faff, not the evening: getting ready, getting there, getting home. Don't count the hours at the party — those are the thing you're buying, and they belong on the enjoyment slider instead. Then two separate questions: would you enjoy it, and does it matter to whoever's asking.

upgradeQuality.title: Buy better, keep longer
upgradeQuality.blurb: Pay more once for something that doesn't need replacing.
upgradeQuality.hint: The price of each and how long each one lasts. That's all — the app works out how many times you'd buy the cheap one, and whether the good one lasts long enough to be worth it. The yearly field is for upkeep, if there is any.

extraWork.title: Extra work vs free time
extraWork.blurb: Overtime, an extra shift, a side project.
extraWork.hint: Use what you'd actually keep after tax, and count the hours you'd be useless afterwards.

unplannedWork.title: Chase the new idea, or not
unplannedWork.blurb: It wasn't the plan for today. It rarely stays an hour.
unplannedWork.hint: Estimate the hours, then double them — this is the decision people misjudge most. Say what the time comes out of: work you've pushed back doesn't disappear, it comes back later with less room. And be honest about whether you'd still do it next week.

squeezeItIn.title: Squeeze it in, or leave it
squeezeItIn.blurb: The gym at eleven at night. The jobs before bed. Now, or tomorrow.
squeezeItIn.hint: Say honestly whether it'll cost you sleep, and whether you'd genuinely do it tomorrow instead. If you would, tonight buys you very little — and sleep is not something to be squeezed around.

dropAnIncome.title: Is this income worth the hours?
dropAnIncome.blurb: A side gig, a client, a rental, a second job. What it pays, against what it takes.
dropAnIncome.hint: What it pays a month, and the hours it really takes a month — the admin, the chasing and the invoicing as well as the work. Then say honestly whether it wipes you out, because the hours it costs you afterwards are the ones nobody counts.

sellStuff.title: Turn stuff into money
sellStuff.hint: The listing is ten minutes. The messages, the packing and the post office are not.

shopAround.title: Shop around
shopAround.blurb: Is the hunt for a better price worth the hours?
shopAround.hint: Put the price you'd realistically end up paying on each side.

diyVsHire.title: DIY vs hire someone
diyVsHire.blurb: Painting, flat-packs, the leaking tap, the website.
diyVsHire.hint: Your estimate of the hours is probably low. It usually is. Then say what you'd come away able to do — a skill you'll use again is worth real money, and one you won't is just a longer way of being busy.

secondHandVsNew.title: Second-hand or new
secondHandVsNew.blurb: The saving is real. So are the evenings spent hunting.
secondHandVsNew.hint: Price on each side, then how long each one lasts — a used one with two years left isn't cheaper than a new one with eight. Put the searching, the messaging and the trip to collect it in the one-off time: you do all of it again every time you replace it.

sellIndividuallyVsBulk.title: Sell one by one, or the lot
sellIndividuallyVsBulk.blurb: More money for far more evenings, against one transaction and done.
sellIndividuallyVsBulk.optionB: Sell the lot in one go
sellIndividuallyVsBulk.hint: Per item it's photos, a listing, the messages, the packing and the post office — enter one item's worth, then say how many. The other side is one transaction and done, so that side is one.

payForAdmin.title: Pay someone to do the admin
payForAdmin.blurb: Tax return, forms, applications, chasing a refund.
payForAdmin.hint: Count the dread as well as the hours — admin you keep putting off costs more than the clock says.

dayOffForAdmin.title: Take a day off to clear it
dayOffForAdmin.blurb: Spend a day's leave doing life admin, or grind through it in the evenings.
dayOffForAdmin.hint: Annual leave is currency too. Evening hours are worth less than they look — you're tired.

babysitterTax.title: A night out, all in
babysitterTax.blurb: A £40 evening is a £110 evening once childcare is in it.
babysitterTax.hint: Put the whole cost in — sitter, travel, the lot. Then be generous on the feel slider, because you should be — and remember it isn't only your evening.

learnItOnce.title: Learn it once, save forever
learnItOnce.blurb: Hours now to learn something that saves you time every week after.
learnItOnce.optionB: Keep doing it the slow way
learnItOnce.hint: Learning goes in the one-off field, the weekly time saved underneath. Look years ahead — this is the one that compounds.

commuteVsRent.title: Commute vs rent
commuteVsRent.blurb: Cheaper further out, or pay more to live close in.
commuteVsRent.hint: Daily travel cost and door-to-door time at the top, then the monthly rent underneath.

fourDayWeek.title: Drop a day a week
fourDayWeek.blurb: Four days instead of five. The purest version of this trade.
fourDayWeek.hint: Monthly take-home on each side, and the hours you'd give back. Look a year or more ahead.

salaryVsCommute.title: More money, longer commute
salaryVsCommute.blurb: A better-paid job that's further away.
salaryVsCommute.hint: Daily travel cost and door-to-door time at the top, then monthly take-home underneath.

childcareVsHours.title: Childcare vs dropping hours
childcareVsHours.blurb: Nursery fees against a parent's hours. Often the biggest sum in a household.
childcareVsHours.hint: Fees minus any free hours or tax-free childcare, against the take-home you'd lose.

trainingForPay.title: Train now, earn later
trainingForPay.blurb: A course or qualification that should pay for itself.
trainingForPay.hint: Fees and study hours up front, then the monthly pay rise underneath. Look several years ahead — and the capability counts as well as the money, which is often the better half of it.

carOwnership.title: Own a car, or don't
carOwnership.blurb: Insurance, tax, MOT, depreciation — against taxis and car clubs.
carOwnership.hint: Everything the car costs per month, including the bit nobody counts: depreciation — and the taxis and car club as a month's worth too, not per trip. Then the lump sum: what selling it would bring, on the right — or the price of buying one, if that's the way round you're asking.

takeALodger.title: Take a lodger
takeALodger.blurb: Rent for privacy. The feel slider matters more than the money here.
takeALodger.hint: Rent received, plus the hours of extra tidying, and what the room costs to get ready in the one-off field — that's what the rent has to pay back first. Then be honest about how it'd feel.
